name: starting architecture
last_analysis: Scores are hidden, so the choice rests on task structure. The footprint-window head (r1c2/r2c2/r3c1) scores each placement from the exact covered cells, which looks like the most fitting design. Recipes with fewer epochs trade data reuse for more fresh designs (307k steps with 1 epoch) and stay inside the time limit. A brick lands on the highest filled cell under its footprint, which needs a max over the covered cells. A linear window conv plus one ReLU computes this poorly, while max/min pooling gives it directly. So a head combining the window conv with pooling is the most promising refinement. For this last round I give the combined head two recipes (2 epochs, and 1 epoch with the legal-action mask as input). The third candidate keeps r3c1's network and tests a longer horizon with lower entropy for sharper greedy play.
